name: Maltese Citizenship by Descent (Birth Abroad / Registration as Descendant)

qualifying_event.description: A person born abroad to a Maltese-citizen parent acquires Maltese citizenship automatically by descent (formal proof via Form D). A person more distantly descended -- in direct line from an ancestor who was born in Malta and whose own parent was likewise born in Malta -- may instead acquire citizenship by registration (Form K, or Form M for minors).
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Birth/marriage certificates establishing the ancestral chain; proof of the relevant ancestor's birth in Malta.

requirement_groups.name: Born abroad to a Maltese-citizen parent

requirements.blocker_text: Automatic citizenship for a person born abroad on or after 1 August 1989 to a parent who was a Maltese citizen at the time of birth; a formal certificate is obtained via Form D.

requirement_groups.name: Registration as descendant of a Malta-born ancestor

requirements.blocker_text: Registration available to a person in direct line of descent from an ancestor born in Malta, where that ancestor's own parent was also born in Malta -- reaching further back than a single Maltese parent (Form K for adults, Form M for minors).

evidence_required.document: Birth/marriage certificates establishing the ancestral chain
Proof of the relevant ancestor's birth in Malta
Application Form D, K, or M as applicable (EUR150 + EUR50 on collection)

sources.title: Agenzija Komunita Malta -- Acquisition of Citizenship: by birth, by registration (descendant, spouse, former citizen), by naturalisation, by naturalisation for exceptional services, and dual/multiple citizenship reacquisition

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Malta's initial build. Confirmed directly at tier-1. IMPORTANT LIMIT flagged by the source itself: citizenship acquired by registration based on descent CANNOT be transmitted to the registrant's own children -- this materially caps how far a distant-descendant claim can cascade across further generations, unlike the automatic by-birth-abroad ground. Tier-3/tier-4 commentary (e.g. IMI Daily) frames 'hundreds of thousands' of foreign nationals as potentially eligible under the registration-descendant ground given Malta's emigration history; that framing is context only, not itself verified at tier-1. Historical eligibility windows differ by birth date (pre-Sept-1964, 1964-1989, post-1989) per the source's fuller 'By Birth' breakdown -- this route models the post-1989 rule as the current-relevance case; older birth-date variants exist but are not separately modelled given they apply to an aging cohort.
